metadata.verificationMethod: Reproduce approval-rate estimates from the frozen loan-application records and compare them across independently chosen market, product, and applicant groupings.

tasks.name: Where Mortgage Applications Succeed
tasks.content: Where are homebuyers most likely to have their mortgage applications approved?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md containing your definition of approval, the comparison groups you chose, application counts and approval rates for each reported group, a concise answer to the question, and any important data limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Recompute denial-reason frequencies and adjusted associations, then test whether the ordering survives alternative treatments of missing, multiple, and inapplicable reasons.

tasks.name: Why Mortgage Applications Are Denied
tasks.content: What seems to distinguish applications that are denied from those that move forward?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md containing the denial and comparison cohorts, the factors and denial reasons examined, supporting statistics or model results, your interpretation, and caveats about missing or multiple denial reasons.

metadata.verificationMethod: Have mortgage-lending experts score the lender assessment against an evidence rubric, inspect counterexamples, and compare conclusions under competing definitions of community service.

tasks.name: Lenders Serving Their Communities
tasks.content: Which lenders appear to serve their local communities particularly well?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a text file named answer.txt identifying the lenders you selected, explaining what community and strong service mean in your analysis, citing the evidence behind the assessment, and discussing at least one plausible alternative interpretation.

metadata.verificationMethod: Independently reconstruct the comparison cohorts and adjusted models, audit overlap and missingness, and verify that reported gaps are robust to reasonable product and geography definitions.

tasks.name: Comparable Applicants and Unequal Outcomes
tasks.content: Do similarly situated applicants receive meaningfully different mortgage outcomes?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md documenting how comparable applicants and outcomes were defined, the adjustment or matching approach, group-level sample sizes and estimates with uncertainty, robustness checks, and a careful statement of what the analysis can and cannot establish.

metadata.verificationMethod: Ask independent domain reviewers to assess the underserved-market ranking, proxy choices, alternative explanations, and actionability; test whether recommendations persist under different normative priorities.

tasks.name: Finding Underserved Mortgage Markets
tasks.content: Which communities seem underserved by the mortgage market, and what might be going wrong?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md containing a ranked shortlist of communities, your definition and indicators of underservice, evidence for each selection, competing explanations, data limitations, and one actionable recommendation for further investigation.

metadata.verificationMethod: Reproduce rating summaries from linked title and ratings records and check whether conclusions survive vote thresholds, title-type splits, and weighted versus unweighted estimates.

tasks.name: Titles Audiences Rate Highly
tasks.content: What kinds of titles tend to receive higher audience ratings?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md containing the title categories and eligibility rules used, rating and vote-count summaries, comparisons supporting your answer, sensitivity to low-vote titles, and key limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Rebuild episode and season trajectories, audit missing episodes and vote coverage, and compare results under several pre-registered definitions of declining enthusiasm.

tasks.name: When Series Lose Momentum
tasks.content: When does a television series seem to lose its audience's enthusiasm?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md defining loss of momentum, describing the eligible series and episode ordering, presenting the observed rating or voting trajectories, identifying representative series, and noting missing-data and selection limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Independently count regional and language aliases, sample-check title linkage, and test rankings under alternative definitions of cross-market reach and minimum title prominence.

tasks.name: Stories That Cross Borders
tasks.content: Which titles seem to travel especially well across languages and regions?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named cross_border_titles.csv with the selected title identifiers, titles, and reach measures, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md explaining the reach definition, filters, ranking method, notable findings, and limitations of using alternate-title records as a proxy.

metadata.verificationMethod: Have film-domain reviewers judge the proposed breakthrough narratives against full career timelines, rejected alternatives, and counterexamples; measure agreement across reviewers.

tasks.name: Recognizing a Career Breakthrough
tasks.content: What does a real career breakthrough look like for people working in film and television?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a text file named answer.txt stating your working definition of a breakthrough, describing the career evidence and examples that shaped it, addressing counterexamples or alternative definitions, and summarizing the limits of the available data.

metadata.verificationMethod: Audit the collaboration graph and then ask independent experts to assess whether the chosen influence concept, role scope, and case interpretations are defensible under competing network definitions.

tasks.name: Influential Creative Collaborators
tasks.content: Who seems unusually influential in shaping creative collaboration networks?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md identifying the collaborators you consider influential, defining the network and influence measure, providing reproducible supporting metrics and illustrative cases, comparing at least one alternative measure, and discussing interpretation limits.

metadata.verificationMethod: Recompute tip rates for eligible trip and payment types, audit zero and missing tips, and compare patterns across time, route, distance, and fare bands.

tasks.name: When Riders Tip More
tasks.content: When do riders tend to leave more generous tips?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md defining the eligible trips and tip measure, reporting trip counts and tip summaries across the conditions examined, answering the question with supporting comparisons, and noting payment-type and data-quality limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Recreate route-level time and price baselines, validate zone joins and trip filters, and confirm flagged routes under robust outlier definitions and comparable trip conditions.

tasks.name: Unexpectedly Slow or Expensive Routes
tasks.content: Which trips or routes are slower or more expensive than a rider might reasonably expect?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named flagged_routes.csv listing each flagged route or trip group and its observed and expected time or cost measures, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md documenting filters, baselines, thresholds, main findings, and limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Independently rerun temporal, geographic, and arithmetic anomaly rules, manually inspect stratified samples, and report precision estimates for each anomaly class.

tasks.name: Suspicious Trip Records
tasks.content: Which trip records look suspicious, and what kinds of data problems might they reveal?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named suspicious_trips.csv containing record identifiers or reproducible row references, anomaly categories, and the values that triggered each flag, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md with detection rules, category counts, manual checks, and false-positive caveats.

metadata.verificationMethod: Have transportation experts review the inferred supply-demand gaps, compare plausible proxy definitions, inspect contradictory zones and hours, and judge whether proposed interpretations exceed the available evidence.

tasks.name: Where Ride Availability Falls Short
tasks.content: Where and when does ride availability seem poorly matched to what travelers need?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md identifying the places and times of concern, defining the supply and need proxies used, presenting supporting evidence, considering contradictory cases and alternative explanations, and distinguishing observations from recommendations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Evaluate the service assessment with an expert rubric covering accessibility, shared-ride matching, wait-time proxies, geographic equity, missing counterfactuals, and alternative interpretations.

tasks.name: How Well Specialized Ride Options Work
tasks.content: How well do shared and accessible ride options appear to work for New Yorkers?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a text file named answer.txt describing how you evaluated shared and accessible services, the metrics and comparisons used, the evidence supporting your assessment, important geographic or temporal differences, and limitations of the available service indicators.

metadata.verificationMethod: Reproduce late-delivery rates after auditing order status, timestamp consistency, missing delivery dates, and the definition of lateness; sample-check extreme cases.

tasks.name: Orders That Arrive Late
tasks.content: Which kinds of orders are most likely to arrive later than promised?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md defining eligible and late orders, reporting order counts and late-delivery rates for the segments examined, highlighting the strongest patterns, and documenting timestamp, status, and missing-data caveats.

metadata.verificationMethod: Rebuild order-level features without join inflation, reproduce review comparisons, and check stability across product, seller, geography, price, and delivery-time controls.

tasks.name: What Leads to Better Reviews
tasks.content: When do customers tend to leave better reviews?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md defining the analysis unit and review outcome, presenting supporting comparisons or model results with sample sizes, explaining the factors associated with better reviews, and addressing join multiplicity, confounding, and missing reviews.

metadata.verificationMethod: Independently reconcile item prices, freight, payments, and order multiplicity, then verify high-burden segments under alternative denominators and treatment of multi-item orders.

tasks.name: Why Shipping Feels Expensive
tasks.content: For which purchases does shipping become unusually expensive relative to what is being bought?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named high_shipping_burden.csv containing the selected orders or segments and their item value, freight cost, and burden measure, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md explaining aggregation choices, thresholds, findings, and multi-item-order caveats.

metadata.verificationMethod: Have marketplace-operations reviewers assess the seller scorecard, inspect borderline sellers, and test whether conclusions persist across reasonable metric weights, minimum-volume rules, and uncertainty adjustments.

tasks.name: Sellers Customers Can Rely On
tasks.content: Which sellers seem to provide consistently strong service?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named seller_scorecard.csv with seller identifiers, eligible order counts, component metrics, and the final assessment, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md explaining metric choices, minimum-volume rules, uncertainty, rankings, and limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Use independent expert scoring of the opportunity rationale, rejected alternatives, operational constraints, proxy validity, and sensitivity to competing growth priorities.

tasks.name: Promising Marketplace Expansion
tasks.content: Where might the marketplace have its most promising room to expand?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md recommending and ranking expansion opportunities, defining the opportunity measures and geographic or product scope, presenting evidence, comparing rejected alternatives, and discussing operational constraints and proxy limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Reconstruct statement totals from numeric facts and presentation relationships, check units and contexts, and compare every flagged inconsistency with the relevant calculation relationships.

tasks.name: Financial Statements That Do Not Add Up
tasks.content: Which reported financial statements contain totals that do not seem to add up?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named statement_issues.csv containing filer, filing, statement, period, reported total, reconstructed total, difference, units, and issue type, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md documenting calculation rules, tolerances, validation checks, and caveats.

metadata.verificationMethod: Independently map revenue and profitability tags, align fiscal contexts and units, reproduce changes, and verify conclusions under conservative and expansive tag mappings.

tasks.name: Companies Improving Profitability
tasks.content: Which companies appear to be improving their profitability, and which are moving the other way?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named profitability_trends.csv with company identifiers, aligned periods, revenue and profitability measures, changes, and trend classification, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md explaining tag mappings, inclusion rules, main findings, and comparability limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Have financial analysts code a sample of narrative disclosures, review the theme synthesis and omitted risks, and measure whether independent reviewers reach similar interpretations.

tasks.name: Risks Companies Are Emphasizing
tasks.content: What risks and uncertainties are companies emphasizing in their disclosures?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a text file named answer.txt summarizing the risk themes you identified, naming representative companies or disclosures for each theme, explaining how themes were derived, noting meaningful variation or counterexamples, and describing coverage and interpretation limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Audit taxonomy mappings, units, periods, dimensions, custom tags, and company selection; reproduce comparability scores and test them against expert-reviewed fact pairs.

tasks.name: Comparing Revenue Across Filers
tasks.content: How comparable are the revenue figures that different companies report?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a CSV file named revenue_comparability.csv containing the compared filers and facts, taxonomy tags, periods, units, dimensions, mapping decisions, and comparability assessment, plus a Markdown file named methodology.md with validation examples, findings, and limitations.

metadata.verificationMethod: Ask independent analysts to assess the resilience ranking, trace every claim to filing evidence, challenge the metric and peer choices, and score the quality of competing interpretations.

tasks.name: Financially Resilient Companies
tasks.content: Which companies look best prepared to withstand financial stress?
tasks.deliverables: Submit a Markdown file named report.md identifying and ranking the companies assessed as resilient, defining the peer set and resilience criteria, tracing each conclusion to filing metrics or disclosures, testing at least one alternative weighting or stress scenario, and discussing uncertainty.
